about: Network tail budgets for tools/performance/net-tail.mts. Each row of the matrix (weapon x profile x RTT) is one deterministic tools/netlab.mts run with the game's two sockets (--aux). A budget applies to the rows its rtt range and profiles name. Proposed by RAY-163 from main's own numbers and agreed 2026-11-05; npm test runs net-tail --check against them (check id nettail). Rows run on each transport in 'transports': ws is the game's two WebSockets (--aux), wt is WebTransport (--transport wt: input windows and snapshots as datagrams). A budget with 'transports' holds only on those; one without holds on every transport. The wt-only budgets (RAY-184 PR 5) hold what datagrams buy on lossy links, from wt's own numbers at 15bb7af.

jitter20.why: a steady home connection: 20 ms of jitter, nothing lost

loss1.why: busy Wi-Fi: 1% of TCP segments lost on each socket and direction, resent after about 1.25 RTT

loss2j40.why: a bad connection: 2% loss and 40 ms of jitter; reported, no budget yet

budgets.why: a hit marker the server then rejects is the worst thing a player feels; 150 ms covers most of North America and Europe to one server
same: no hit marker the server rejects
netlab --check already holds this on a steady link up to 250 ms

no hit marker the server rejects on slow links either: while the link stalls, or above about 220 ms of RTT on a rough link, the client shows no predicted hit and the server's verdict draws the marker (ClientMatch.linkSlow, KONG-78 2b)
a steady link keeps its instant hit markers up to 250 ms: at most 1% of hits wait for the server (KONG-78 §4 2b's gate); the wait is for stalled, rough or past-the-rewind-cap links only
p99 never misses more than one 30 Hz snapshot in a row; the redundant socket is what keeps this true under loss
the server's own share of input→first ack (queue, the next tick, the next 30 Hz snapshot, jitter) stays within 3 ticks on a steady link; main is 37.5-41.7 ms
with 1% loss a resent input costs up to one more RTT on one socket; two sockets keep the p99 near the steady case (main: 65.3-72.2 ms at ≤150 ms)
rubber-banding: under 5% of snapshots correct the local prediction (perf-state target)
enemies freeze on screen when interpolation runs dry; under 2% of frames
on datagrams a lost input is carried by the next window instead of waiting for a resend, so 1% loss keeps the steady link's budget up to 250 ms (wt: 40.3-44.4 ms; ws: 65.3-204 ms)
a bad connection (2% loss, 40 ms jitter) stays within about 3.5 ticks on datagrams (wt: 48.6-54.2 ms; ws: 54-299 ms)
with 1% loss the link never stalls on datagrams, so hit markers stay instant up to 250 ms (wt: 0; ws: 24-32% at 250 ms)
and the instant markers are real: the server confirms them (wt: 100%)
